newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian ATX hits record high, consolidation seen.
newsitem.headline: Austrian ATX hits record high, consolidation seen.

text.p: Austrian shares rallied to a record closing high on Wednesday up 1.93 percent at 1,365.75, but traders predicted that the market would see some consolidation before it could extend the gains further.
"It's all going a bit fast. It would be good to have a breather," said one trader.

The blue chip ATX steamed higher to end 24.88 points or 1.86 percent up at 1,364.75 but came off a record intraday high of 1,374.99 after profit-taking set in. Among its constituents 19 shares rose and two fell.
Traders said foreign investors had pumped a lot of money into the futures market which is currently traded over the "fair value".
However, in Austria the strong gains of the last few days -- over 70 points or 5.5 percent this week -- had given rise to sceptism as to whether the rally could be sustained, dealers said.
"There's been quite a lot of profit-taking. I doubt we will make 1,400 in one go," one trader said.
Many said they would welcome a correction to about 1,340 to 1,350 points. The next short-term goal is seen as 1,400.
Microchip maker AMS led the gainers, jumping 6.11 percent to 1,112 schillings.
The day's leading loser was luxury hosiery maker Wolford, which slid 2.76 percent to 1,235 schillings.
The July ATX future rose 23.5 points to 1,370.5.
